title: Plans that make multi-line output
idea: A multi-step plan produces multi-line output. Match each plan step to the line it prints.

exercises.prompt: A plan has 3 show-steps. How many lines will appear on screen?
exercises.explanation: Each print line shows its text on its own line. Three steps make three lines of output.

exercises.prompt:
Code:
print("Line one")
print("Line two")
What appears on screen?
options: Line one on the first line, Line two on the second
exercises.explanation: Each print starts a new line. So you get two separate lines of output.

exercises.prompt: Each separate print line shows its text on its own line.
exercises.explanation: Yes. That's why a 3-step plan gives tidy, 3-line output — one line per step.

exercises.prompt:
You want output:
Hello
World
Order the code lines.
exercises.explanation: Hello line first, World line second — the output appears in the order the code runs.

exercises.prompt: Plan: show a name, then an age, each on its own line. How many print lines?
exercises.explanation: Two things, each on its own line, means two print lines.

exercises.prompt: Match each plan step to the line it prints.
exercises.explanation: Each plan step maps to one print line. Together they make three lines of output.

exercises.prompt:
Output on screen:
Start
Middle
End
How many print lines made this?
options: It can't be done with print
exercises.explanation: Three lines of output come from three print lines, one per line.

exercises.prompt: Task: show a menu. Output should read Starter, Main, Dessert. Order the code.
exercises.explanation: Starter, Main, Dessert — the plan's order becomes the output's order.

exercises.prompt: Swapping two print lines swaps which line appears first on screen.
exercises.explanation: Yes. The code runs top to bottom, so line order decides output order.

exercises.prompt: Plan: show Welcome, then show the date, then show Enjoy. What will the output look like?
options: Three lines: Welcome, the date, Enjoy
exercises.explanation: Three steps, three print lines, three lines of output in order. You can picture output before running it!
